The core operators define a type system as a structured set of font assets with metadata, license, and rendering properties. The authority manifold enforces that user fonts are validated before use, ensuring deterministic behavior in GSE. The Google Fonts system acts as a derived kernel, offering recommendations under constraint. Type pair determinism ensures that once a pair is approved, it becomes a fixed point in the Brandkit state. Dualities emerge in that user fonts are authoritative yet must comply with licensing, while Google Fonts are heuristic yet must satisfy design constraints. Failure modes include unvalidated fonts leading to rendering errors, or non-compliant pairs causing legal issues. The system avoids over-engineering by limiting scope to two families and deterministic rendering.
